newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS- US markets give budget pact modest applause.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS- US markets give budget pact modest applause.

text.p: Bonds popped higher and stocks jumped in late trading after news of an agreement on Friday between the Clinton administration and congressional Republicans to balance the budget by 2002.

But market analysts cautioned that the initial market reaction could be deceiving. Given that expectations of a deal had been coursing through the markets for several weeks, they predicted limited additional gains in the near-term.
Market participants also stressed that much work remains to be done on a budget which has yet to be approved -- or even reviewed -- by other key members of Congress.

"I think what the market likes about it is that it is only May and the White House and the conservative Republicans are in agreement on at least the broad brush strokes," said Christopher Low, senior economist at HSBC Markets Inc.

"But it's also just beginning to sink in that while this is a deal that included Trent Lott and Newt Gingrich and the White House, it excluded an awful lot of people, including all the senior Democrats in the House and Senate," he added.
